messages.subject: Introduced nan bug?
parts:
When running my current model, the last value of a sampled parameter seems to be being changed to nan at some point. I have a print statement for the relevant vector, which gives the following:

[6.9325,4.33623,3.50451,7.96258,3.26908,8.39752,4.6855,7.79741,8.60823,4.93992,7.90553,8.33216,1.79585,1.51152,1.88836,7.94581]
[6.9325,4.33623,3.50451,7.96258,3.26908,8.39752,4.6855,7.79741,8.60823,4.93992,7.90553,8.33216,1.79585,1.51152,1.88836,-nan]

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
Invalid value of intercept: validate transformed params(N4stan5agrad3varE): intercept is -nan:0, but must be greater than or equal to 0

I have to say I do not understand why the print statement is being called twice, as I only have it once in transformed parameters.

Here is the relevant code:

parameters{
real<lower=1,upper=5000> DNAcont[n_gen/2];
real<lower=0,upper=1> degradation[n_gen/2];
real<lower=0,upper=10000> scale;
real<lower=0,upper=0.01> gradientS;
vector<lower=0.1,upper=10>[n_loc] gradientAdjust;
real<lower=0,upper=0.01> interceptS;
vector<lower=0.1,upper=10>[n_loc] interceptAdjust;
real<lower=0> repAdjust[n_rep-1];
real<lower=0,upper=0.1> meanD;
real<lower=0,upper=0.1> meanO;
//vector outGenProbs[sum_n_combs];
}

transformed parameters{
real<lower=0> intercept;
real<lower=0> gradient; 
vector<lower=0,upper=1>[sum_n_frags] stutterRateData;
//vector<lower=0,upper=1>[sum_n_frags] overallStutter;
print(interceptAdjust);
for(i in 1:sum_n_frags)
{
intercept <- interceptS*interceptAdjust[fragIndex[i]];
gradient <- gradientS*gradientAdjust[fragIndex[i]];
stutterRateData[i] <- intercept+(gradient*LUSvalsData[i]);
}
}

model {
...
// priors
gradientAdjust ~ lognormal(0,0.15);
interceptAdjust ~ lognormal(0,0.5);
meanD ~ gamma(0.02/0.018,0.018);
meanO ~ gamma(0.02/0.018,0.018);
degradation ~ exponential(500);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Introduced nan bug?
parts:
It gets called every evaluation of the log density function, which can
happen multiple times per iteration. Those super fat priors

> real<lower=1,upper=5000> DNAcont[n_gen/2];

are causing DNAcont to be initialized around 2500 --- it takes the midpoint
of an upper-and-lower-bounded variable. So unless 2500 is a reasonable value
for this variable, you want a more sensible constraint, like something just
constrained to be positive (or above 1) with a softer constraint.

- Bob
